items.sentence_raw: The concept of health holds different meanings for different people and groups.
These meanings of health have also changed over time.
This change is no more evident than in Western society today, when notions of health and health promotion are being challenged and expanded in new ways.
items.explain: Q14: The passage says *'notions of health and health promotion are being challenged and expanded in new ways'* — this means ideas about health are **changing**. The heading **viii** (*'Changes in concepts of health in Western society'*) matches this idea of **change**. So the answer is **viii**.

items.sentence_raw: For much of recent Western history, health has been viewed in the physical sense only.
That is, good health has been connected to the smooth mechanical operation of the body, while ill health has been attributed to a breakdown in this machine.
Health in this sense has been defined as the absence of disease or illness and is seen in medical terms.
According to this view, creating health for people means providing medical care to treat or prevent disease and illness.
During this period, there was an emphasis on providing clean water, improved sanitation and housing.
In the late 1940s the World Health Organisation challenged this physically and medically oriented view of health.
They stated that "health is a complete state of physical, mental and social well-being and is not merely the absence of disease" (WHO, 1946).
items.explain: Q19: The passage quotes the WHO definition and then gives the source as *'(WHO, 1946)'* — the year is right there in brackets. So the answer is **1946**.

items.sentence_raw: Health and the person were seen more holistically (mind / body / spirit) and not just in physical terms.
items.explain: Q15: The passage says health was seen *'more holistically (mind / body / spirit)'* — **'holistically'** means looking at the whole person, not just the body. The heading **ii** (*'Holistic approach to health'*) uses the exact same key word. So the answer is **ii**.

items.sentence_raw: The 1970s was a time of focusing on the prevention of disease and illness by emphasising the importance of the lifestyle and behaviour of the individual.
items.explain:
Q16: The passage says the 1970s focused on *'the lifestyle and behaviour of the individual'* to prevent disease. The heading **iv** (*'Healthy lifestyles approach to health'*) directly names this **lifestyle** focus. So the answer is **iv**.

Q22: The passage states *'The 1970s was a time of focusing on... the lifestyle and behaviour of the individual'* — this directly links **lifestyle risks** to that decade. So the answer is **the 1970s**.

items.sentence_raw: Specific behaviours which were seen to increase risk of disease, such as smoking, lack of fitness and unhealthy eating habits, were targeted.
Creating health meant providing not only medical health care, but health promotion programs and policies which would help people maintain healthy behaviours and lifestyles.
items.explain: Q24: The passage says creating health in the 1970s meant providing *'health promotion programs and policies'* — **'health promotion programs'** means **health awareness programs**. The question says these were *'introduced'*, which matches the passage. So the answer is **YES**.

items.sentence_raw: While this individualistic healthy lifestyles approach to health worked for some (the wealthy members of society), people experiencing poverty, unemployment, underemployment or little control over the conditions of their daily lives benefited little from this approach.
items.explain: Q20: The passage says the healthy lifestyles approach *'worked for some (the wealthy members of society)'* — the brackets tell you exactly who benefited. So the answer is **the wealthy members**.

items.sentence_raw: This was largely because both the healthy lifestyles approach and the medical approach to health largely ignored the social and environmental conditions affecting the health of people.
During the 1980s and 1990s there has been a growing swing away from seeing lifestyle risks as the root cause of poor health.
While lifestyle factors still remain important, health is being viewed also in terms of the social, economic and environmental contexts in which people live.
items.explain: Q21: The passage says health is viewed in terms of *'the social, economic and environmental contexts'* — these are the three broad areas. So the answer is **social, economic, environmental**.

items.sentence_raw: This broad approach to health is called the socio-ecological view of health.
items.explain: Q17: The passage directly states *'This broad approach to health is called the socio-ecological view of health'*. The heading **ix** (*'Socio-ecological view of health'*) is an exact match. So the answer is **ix**.

items.sentence_raw: The broad socio-ecological view of health was endorsed at the first International Conference of Health Promotion held in 1986, Ottawa, Canada, where people from 38 countries agreed and declared that:
"The fundamental conditions and resources for health are peace, shelter, education, food, a viable income, a stable eco-system, sustainable resources, social justice and equity.
Improvement in health requires a secure foundation in these basic requirements.
It is clear from this statement that the creation of health is about much more than encouraging healthy individual behaviours and lifestyles and providing appropriate medical care.
items.explain: Q25: The passage says creating health is *'about much more than encouraging healthy individual behaviours and lifestyles and providing appropriate medical care'*. This means lifestyle and medical care are **not** the only critical factors — the question says they **are** critical. These ideas conflict, so the answer is **NO**.

items.sentence_raw: Therefore, the creation of health must include addressing issues such as poverty, pollution, urbanisation, natural resource depletion, social alienation and poor working conditions.
The social, economic and environmental contexts which contribute to the creation of health do not operate separately or independently of each other.
Rather, they are interacting and interdependent, and it is the complex interrelationships between them which determine the conditions that promote health.
A broad socio-ecological view of health suggests that the promotion of health must include a strong social, economic and environmental focus.
At the Ottawa Conference in 1986, a charter was developed which outlined new directions for health promotion based on the socio-ecological view of health.
This charter, known as the Ottawa Charter for Health Promotion, remains as the backbone of health action today.
items.explain:
Q18: The passage says *'This charter, known as the Ottawa Charter for Health Promotion, remains as the backbone of health action today'*. The heading **vii** (*'Ottawa Charter for Health Promotion'*) names this exact charter. So the answer is **vii**.

Q26: The passage says the Ottawa Charter *'remains as the backbone of health action today'* — **'remains'** means it is still important, not out of date. The question says the principles are *'out of date'*, which is the opposite. So the answer is **NO**.

items.sentence_raw: In exploring the scope of health promotion it states that:
"Good health is a major resource for social, economic and personal development and an important dimension of quality of life.
Political, economic, social, cultural, environmental, behavioural and biological factors can all favour health or be harmful to it.
The Ottawa Charter brings practical meaning and action to this broad notion of health promotion.
It presents fundamental strategies and approaches in achieving health for all.
The overall philosophy of health promotion which guides these fundamental strategies and approaches is one of "enabling people to increase control over and to improve their health" (WHO, 1986).

orphan_explain_map.23: Q23: The passage discusses medical care and living standards like clean water and housing, but it never says **doctors** were *'instrumental'* in improving them. The role of doctors is simply not mentioned. ***NOT GIVEN is not the same as FALSE*** — so the answer is **NOT GIVEN**.
orphan_explain_map.27: Q27: The passage mentions the 1986 conference had people from 38 countries, but it says nothing about **additional countries** joining in *'recent years'*. This information about new subscribers is completely missing. ***Do not confuse the 1986 event with recent years*** — so the answer is **NOT GIVEN**.
